subject: learning/forgejo-native-task-code-and-lifecycle-identity
statement: Native Forgejo task projection, execution, pull-request state, feedback, lane handling, and wake processing carry provider/server/repository-qualified identities through the existing ports. Native issue and comment identifiers survive reloads, while claims and task-session state separate identical numeric IDs from different hosts.
intent: Run the same feature-development lifecycle on either forge without misrouting work, reusing another repository's claim, duplicating feedback, or treating stale checks as proof for the current head.
rationale: Forgejo's GitHub-like object shapes do not make owner/name plus issue number globally unique. Native dependencies, label filters, draft proposals, reviews, effective branch rules, and failed Actions logs require provider-specific interpretation and readback. Unknown capability, malformed state, moving heads, partial reads, or unavailable identity must remain errors rather than manufacture a green or completed result.
fit_criterion: The shared task-capsule conformance suite passes on Forgejo; concurrent hierarchy updates retain both edges; equal issue numbers on distinct task hosts receive separate claims; comments and review feedback retain native identities; checks and failed logs select the latest evidence at the exact proposal head; durable wake resolution uses the selected host and exact object.

provenance.note: Retarget code associations after the port-axis adapter move.
